newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end lower on firmer yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end lower on firmer yen.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures settled lower across the board on Monday reflecting the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar, but falls in prices were offset by bargain-hunting, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from seven to nine yen per gram lower, with benchmark October finishing down eight yen at 1,345 yen.
"Private investors hunted for bargains throughout the day, while trade houses sold futures while buying spot gold in arbitrage trade," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $380.15/45 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $380.05/380.55 in New York on Friday.
Traders said general sluggishness in other commodity futures at home was partly the reason behind private investors' bargain-hunting buying.
In the spot gold market, overseas investors were slightly on the selling side, which was countered by Japan's trade houses' buying.
"Sentiment in gold remains bearish as long as U.S. stock market is strong," a senior dealer at a foreign bank said.
"Persistent rises in U.S. stocks reminds me of Japan's bubble era. We are praying for a correction in U.S. stocks for a possible money shift by investment funds to gold," he said.
Platinum futures ended generally lower in tandem with gold, while silver futures ended firmer, as strong spot silver prices on Friday offset the yen's firmer tendency, the traders said.
One trader said, however, spot silver was still vulnerable to the downside risk.
Most-active benchmark platinum October contract was four yen per gram lower at 1,372 yen. Benchmark October silver contract was 1.2 yen per 10 grams higher at 178.4 yen.
Palladium futures were mixed in directionless trade. Benchmark October palladium was two yen down at 428 yen.
